programs.title: Border Security - Australia's Front Line
programs.desc: The man who smelt too much: Customs and Immigration are faced with a situation that is really on the nose.  A passenger has flown in from Prague, and he has a couple of issues with personal hygiene.  As he has little money and no clothing, Immigration decides to make this man take a shower, buy him some clean clothes and send him back to Prague that afternoon./ Chilean Coke: As a passenger heads towards the baggage carousel, Customs officers suspect that he has something to hide.  At the barriers, the man is agitated as his bags are search and ion scanned for narcotics. The ion scans return a high reading of cocaine.  The bag is X-rayed and reveals a hidden compartment full of an unknown substance in the bottom of his bag.  The Customs dog unit is called to see how the dog will react to the bag.  Within seconds, the dog sits - a positive reaction to narcotics. The AFP is called, and the man is taken away for further questioning./ Cocaine Man: A passenger is nervous at the baggage carou.
